theorem.statement: For every pair \((A,B)\) of normalized nonnegative \(2\times2\) probability tables for which \(F(A,B)\ne\varnothing\), and every \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), the handle \(Hthr\) constructs a finite model \(M\in MC(A,B)\) with binary-valued roots \(U0,V0\) (possibly degenerate), a private root \(W0\) with at most eight support points, mutually independent roots, and one deterministic outcome function \(fY\) shared by all regimes, such that \(q=a+b-c+d\).  The construction reproduces all four cells of \(A\) and all four cells of \(B\).
theorem.justification: The common threshold construction proves that every feasible mass pair, including those on structural-zero faces, lifts without coupling the two source roots.
theorem.gap: Generic finite canonicalization does not itself provide this eight-point source-preserving certificate or its explicit zero-denominator branches.
theorem.consumer: The theorem supplies common-SCM attainment for compatibility, sharpness, exact endpoint certificates, and the fixed-graph analytic dispatch.
theorem.proof_tex: This is exactly the claim of thm:source-preserving-lift-closed-simplex; apply thm:source-preserving-lift-closed-simplex.
